title: Input-Insensitive Machines Are Oblivious
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, let $z\in A$, and let $P$ be a finite-state-set Turing machine over $A$. Suppose that for every state $q$, optional input symbol $s$, and tuple $w$ of work-tape reads, the transition of $P$ on input symbol obtained from $s$ by replacing each present symbol by $z$ is the same as its transition on $s$. Then for any two inputs of equal length and every time $t$, the input-head positions and the tuples of work-tape head positions of the configurations reached after $t$ steps are equal.
hypotheses_covered: Alphabet A and distinguished symbol z ∈ A
Transition invariance for every state, optional input symbol, and work-tape read tuple
replaced:
Let $P$ be a machine over an alphabet $A$ and let $z \in A$. Suppose the transition
table of $P$ is insensitive to nonblank input contents: for every state $q$, scanned
input symbol $s$, and tuple of work-tape reads $w$, the transition of $P$ on the read
obtained from $s$ by replacing any nonblank symbol with $z$ coincides with the
transition of $P$ on $s$ itself. Then $P$ is oblivious.
